newsitem.title: POLAND: FLOODS TO LEAVE SMALL MARK ON POLISH GRAIN OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: FLOODS TO LEAVE SMALL MARK ON POLISH GRAIN OUTPUT.

text.p: Poland's grain output forecasts will be lowered slightly by recent flooding in its wheat-rich south-western regions, but on Tuesday analysts said losses would be contained if the rain stopped soon.
Analysts had forecast this year's grain output to be roughly equal or just lower than the 24.7 million tonnes in 1996, with estimates ranging from about 23.5 to 25 million.

"It seems that forecasts of the grain harvest falling some two to three percent are realistic, with much larger falls in output not probable despite all this rain," Andrzej Kalicki, analyst at the Warsaw Commodities Exchange told Reuters.
However, analysts said that if the rain persisted and floods continued, output could be significantly curbed.

"Flooding will cause losses in the southwest, but it is too early to put an exact figure on it," said a grain analyst, adding that if weather patterns returned to the norm losses should amount to less than five percent.
A spokesman for the agriculture ministry told Reuters that no official crop loss estimates would be given until water levels dropped and fields were examined, which could take days.
Over the last several days heavy downpours caused flooding in many parts of southern Poland, cutting off roads and killing at least four people, while causing hundreds to be evacuated.
